title: Fetch–decode–execute
hook: The CPU does the same 3 steps again and again: get a command, read it, do it.

steps.caption: Step 1 — Fetch: get the next command from memory.

nodeCaptions.mem: Memory holds the list of commands.
nodeCaptions.fetch: Fetch means: pull the next command in.

steps.caption: Step 2 — Decode: figure out what that command means.

nodeCaptions.decode: Decode means: turn the bits into “add”, “copy”, or another action.

steps.caption: Step 3 — Execute: do the work. Then go back to Fetch for the next command.

nodeCaptions.execute: Execute means: actually do the action.
nodeCaptions.mem: Then the loop starts again — billions of times each second.

takeaways: The CPU repeats: Fetch → Decode → Execute.
Fetch = get the next command. Decode = read it. Execute = do it.
Your apps run because this loop never stops.

quiz.question: What are the 3 steps the CPU repeats?
What does Fetch mean?
choices: Get the next command from memory
quiz.explanation: Fetch pulls the next command from memory.

quiz.question: After Execute, what happens next?
choices: It goes back and Fetches the next command
quiz.explanation: The loop continues: fetch the next command and keep going.
